items.title: Tony Fernandes Pushes AirAsia’s Comeback to 2028
items.summary: Tony Fernandes now says 2027 will be a year of consolidation for AirAsia, two months after the airline group promised a fourth-quarter capacity rebound. Engines, not just fuel, are keeping aircraft on the ground.

items.title: Disney’s Epic Games Stake Rises to 10% as It Ties Parks to Fortnite
items.summary: CEO Josh D’Amaro highlighted a Fortnite tie-in as a prime example of how Disney can connect theme parks to its digital business. The company's annual filing reveals a larger stake in Epic Games in fiscal 2026.

items.title: Abu Dhabi Holds Its F1 Hotel Rates as Doha Cuts
items.summary: Abu Dhabi is defending its F1 rate premium on a thinner base of bookings, while Doha has already cut. Late, local-heavy demand will decide whether that holds or forces last-minute discounting.

items.title: Air India Express Names Finance Chief as CEO to Turn Growth Into Profit
items.summary: Air India and Air India Express now both have new CEOs, and the group’s transformation looks steadier for it. The harder test is whether the new leaders can cut losses that are still running in the billions.

items.title: Climate Change Could Squeeze a Third of Tourist Destinations by 2050
items.summary: Climate change won’t just bring more extreme weather. It will shorten the seasons and change the activities many destinations are built on. Operators should be planning now for shoulder seasons and cooler-hour itineraries, not waiting for the next heat wave.

items.title: Airlines Race to Keep Up With Vietnam’s Indian Travel Boom
items.summary: Indian arrivals to Vietnam are growing more than twice as fast as the overall market, and Vietnamese carriers are chasing that demand into cities like Ahmedabad. Seats alone won’t lock it in, though. Vietnam still needs the food, guides, and wedding and events products Indian tra

items.title: Klook’s AI Agent Handles the Admin, but Operators Want Help Selling
items.summary: Klook’s K.ai doesn’t just advise small operators. It makes the changes for them, and an early user says it is already saving time. The bigger payoff, for operators and for Klook, could come from the tools still in development, such as pricing advice that helps them sell more.

items.title: Accor’s $1.8 Billion Ennismore Buyout Tops 4 Rival Lifestyle Deals Combined
items.summary: Hotel groups have spent years buying lifestyle brands. Accor just committed $1.8 billion to buyout the minority investors in its Ennismore joint venture. A comparison with past deals adds some enlightening context.
